question: An engineer configures a storage environment for a customer with high-security standards. The secure environment is configured in VSAN 50. The customer wants to maintain a configuration and active databases and prevent unauthorized switches from joining the fabric. Additionally, the switches must prevent rogue devices from connecting to their ports by automatically learning the WWPNs of the ports connected to them for the first time. Which two configuration sets must be used to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
options: clear fabric-binding activate vsan 50 / fabric-binding activate vsan 50
theory: Combining port-security enable / port-security activate vsan 50 with fabric-binding activate vsan 50 force addresses both stated needs: port security's auto-learning captures the WWPNs of devices connecting to a port for the first time and blocks unrecognized devices thereafter, while fabric binding maintains a switch-level authorized list (verified via EFMD) to keep unauthorized switches from joining the fabric. The force keyword is typically needed the first time fabric binding is activated because already-logged-in switches may conflict with an as-yet-unpopulated fabric-binding database. (CCNP/CCIE DCCOR Official Cert Guide, Chapter 20 - Fabric Binding and Port Security)
